title: Notes on d-matching polynomials, gcd-matrix permanents, and partition self-divisibility, with Lean 4 formalizations
description: Four notes in combinatorics and number theory, with a methodology note, by Vico Bonfioli, each paired with a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization. FINAL RELEASE, and it carries a CORRECTION to releases v5.0 through v5.2. (1) Roots of d-matching polynomials and the spectrum of the universal cover. Hall-Puder-Sawin place the roots of mu_{d,G} in an interval; we conjectured they lie in the spectrum of the universal cover itself, the matching-polynomial form of their Question 6.3. That conjecture is FALSE, by a 41-vertex counterexample due to Chris Hall, verified here independently. Releases v5.0 to v5.2 further claimed that the two proposed repairs, minimum degree three and 3-connectivity, were also refuted here on 14 and 23 vertices; THAT CLAIM IS RETRACTED. In both graphs the root is an eigenvalue of the universal cover, so it lies inside the spectrum. Both repairs are OPEN. What replaces the claim is a theorem in the opposite direction: a separator of size k met by p identical tree branches forces A^(p-k) to divide mu_G, but when p > k the branch union is a theta-Aomoto subset in the sense of Banks-Garza-Vargas-Mukherjee, so the root produced is an eigenvalue of the cover. The condition p > k that makes the divisor nontrivial is exactly the Aomoto inequality, so the branch mechanism can never produce a counterexample. This also explains the pendant leaves in Hall's family, which create the root and simultaneously double the boundary of the relevant star. What stands unaffected is the closed form for mu_{d,G} at first Betti number one, for every d, with the roots located exactly in the spectrum of the cover. (2) The permanent of the gcd matrix a(n)=per[gcd(i,j)] (OEIS A085244), whose arithmetic appears unstudied although the determinant is classical (Smith, 1876): a family of congruences, v2(a(n)) tending to infinity, and (a(n)/n!)^(1/n) tending to infinity unconditionally. The 2-adic deficit is stratified by a class-number ladder of depth exactly three; that result is conditional and concerns the weight-zero grade rather than a(n) itself. (3) Coefficient stability of d-matching polynomials. (4) Integers n with n dividing p(n)-1: a minor note on OEIS A128836, already published complete to 10^8 and recomputed here only to 10^6; read it as a case study, not a result.
